description: Vermont-only rules checked against the Vermont Statutes and the Department of Motor Vehicles. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines. Section 23 V.S.A. 1081 states a 50 mph maximum unless another limit is set; a separate interstate number was not taken from that section.

questions.q: Without an engineering and traffic investigation, a Vermont legislative body may set the maximum on an unpaved town highway at
questions.explanation: Section 23 V.S.A. 1007 says that for unpaved town highways the legislative body may set a maximum of not more than 50 miles per hour and not less than 35 miles per hour without an engineering and traffic investigation, after considering neighborhood character, abutting land use, bicycle and pedestrian use, and the physical characteristics of the highway.

questions.q: A person operating a commercial vehicle in Vermont is prohibited from doing so at an alcohol concentration of
questions.explanation: Section 23 V.S.A. 1201(a)(1)(C) sets 0.04 or more when the person is operating a commercial vehicle as defined in subdivision 4103(4). Subdivision (a)(1)(B) sets 0.02 or more when the person is operating a school bus.

questions.q: A person age 12 or older and under 21 may not operate a vehicle on a Vermont highway when the blood alcohol concentration is
options: 0.00 only if the driver is under 16
questions.explanation: Section 7 V.S.A. 656(b)(1)(E) says a person 12 or older and under 21 shall not operate, attempt to operate, or be in actual physical control of a vehicle on a highway when the person's blood alcohol concentration is 0.02 or more. The former motor-vehicle section 23 V.S.A. 1216 was repealed effective July 1, 2025.

questions.q: After a second or subsequent Vermont conviction under section 1201 in which the alcohol concentration was 0.16 or more, the person may not drive for three years from that conviction at a concentration of
questions.explanation: Section 23 V.S.A. 1201(d)(1) says a person convicted of a second or subsequent violation of subsection (a), (b), or (c), when the alcohol concentration is proven to be 0.16 or more, shall not, for three years from the date of that conviction, operate, attempt to operate, or be in actual physical control of a vehicle on a highway when the alcohol concentration is 0.02 or more. The prohibition is in addition to any other penalties. It is not a rule for every first conviction.

questions.q: On the Vermont graduated-license page, points accumulation that recalls a learner permit or junior license is described as
options: 10 points in two years, for 30 days
questions.explanation: The graduated-license page lists recall of a learner permit or junior driver's license for points accumulation, specifically a single 3-point speeding violation or a 6-point total, for 90 days. A diversion or reparative board recommendation is listed as a 30-day recall.

questions.q: Vermont's published 6-point and 3-point speeding recalls apply to
options: Every adult license, for one year
questions.explanation: The Department of Motor Vehicles states the 90-day recall for a three-point speeding violation or six accumulated points as a recall of a learner's permit or junior operator's license under 23 V.S.A. 607a. The pages opened did not state a separate adult demerit total.

questions.q: A person must possess a Vermont learner's permit for at least how long before a junior driver's license?
questions.explanation: The Department of Motor Vehicles says an individual must possess a learner's permit for at least one year before obtaining a junior driver's license. Its license overview says a learner's permit is available to residents aged 15 or older.

questions.q: Before a Vermont junior driver's license, the applicant must complete additional practice of
options: 40 hours behind the wheel, at least 10 of them at night
No logged hours if driver education is finished
questions.explanation: The graduated-license page says that before a junior driver's license the individual must complete an additional forty hours of practice, with at least ten hours of nighttime driving. The supervising driver described on that page is a licensed and unimpaired individual who is at least 25.

questions.q: During the second three months of a Vermont junior driver's license, the passenger rule allows the driver to begin transporting
questions.explanation: The graduated-license page says that during the second three months the junior driver may begin transporting immediate family members (siblings). After the junior license has been held for six months, there are no passenger restrictions. During the first three months the driver is restricted to driving alone or with one of the supervising individuals indicated on the page.

questions.q: A Vermont driver's license, as distinct from a junior license, requires the person to be 18 and
options: To have no recalls or suspensions in 6 months
To have held a learner permit for 30 days
To have zero passengers for another year
questions.explanation: The graduated-license page says an individual must be 18 to obtain a driver's license and must not have had any recalls, suspensions, or revocations during the previous six-month period. A junior license also requires a clean record, with no learner-permit recalls, suspensions, or revocations, for six months before it is issued.

questions.q: The supervising driver described on Vermont's graduated-license page must be a licensed, unimpaired person who is at least
questions.explanation: The Department of Motor Vehicles says the person accompanying the learner is a licensed and unimpaired individual who is at least 25 years of age.

questions.q: In Vermont, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Vermont issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Vermont car permit: 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Vermont, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Vermont requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 12 months.

questions.q: Of a Vermont teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Vermont requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Vermont: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

questions.q: In Vermont, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Vermont, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: In Vermont, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Vermont drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Vermont car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Vermont car knowledge test has 20 questions.

provenance.manual: Driver's License Manual | Department of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Vermont car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Vermont car knowledge test.

provenance.manual: Driver's License Manual | Department of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: In Vermont, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Vermont, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Vermont, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

questions.q: In Vermont, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Vermont brings a suspension of 180 days.
questions.remember: Vermont, first refusal: 180 days without a license.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Vermont?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Vermont can be posted up to 65 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Vermont rural interstate: up to 65 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Vermont's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
questions.explanation: Vermont: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

provenance.manual: 23 V.S.A. § 1095b. Handheld use of portable electronic device prohibited

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Vermont?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Vermont, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Vermont left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

questions.q: How is Vermont's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: Vermont seat belt enforcement is secondary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Vermont?
questions.explanation: Vermont requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Vermont: car or booster seat until 8 years.

provenance.manual: 23 V.S.A. § 1258. Child restraint systems; individuals under 18 years of age

questions.q: What is Vermont's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Vermont requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $10,000.

questions.q: Under Vermont's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Vermont can suspend an adult's license at 10 points in 24 months.

provenance.manual: 23 V.S.A. § 2505. Suspension or revocation of license
